claims.text: As-received Q235 mild steel contains manufacturing-induced residual stresses.
Annealing Q235 steel at approximately 600 °C for 2 hours minimizes its residual stresses.
Residual stresses promote micro-crack formation in oxide scales during cyclic high-temperature salt exposure.
The density and connectivity of oxide-scale micro-cracks are governed by the residual-stress state.
Oxide-scale micro-cracks create pathways for aggressive salt ions to reach the Q235 substrate.
Salt ingress through oxide-scale cracks accelerates localized corrosion.
Stress relief produces a more coherent, uniform, and mechanically resilient oxide layer on Q235 steel.
A more coherent oxide layer better inhibits corrosion during cyclic high-temperature salt exposure.
Under cyclic salt exposure at 700–900 °C, as-received Q235 will exhibit more oxide-scale micro-cracking than stress-relieved Q235.
Under cyclic salt exposure at 700–900 °C, as-received Q235 will exhibit greater mass change than stress-relieved Q235.
Under cyclic salt exposure at 700–900 °C, as-received Q235 will corrode faster than stress-relieved Q235.
At room temperature, thermal stresses are minimal relative to those generated during high-temperature cycling.
The room-temperature corrosion behavior of as-received and stress-relieved Q235 should differ negligibly.
The proposed mechanism should apply when significant thermal cycling and salt exposure occur at 700–900 °C.
The proposed mechanism may not apply in inert or low-temperature environments where oxide-scale formation and thermal-stress effects are minimal.
Grain size, phase composition, and oxide chemistry may independently affect corrosion behavior and confound the residual-stress comparison.

Cracks observed in HEA coatings on carbon- and stainless-steel substrates were attributed tentatively to manufacturing, deposition, thermal input, thermal-property mismatch, internal stress, or coating hardness.
A Cr18Mn27Fe27.5Ni27.5 high-entropy alloy was exposed to molten FLiBe at 700 °C for 1000 hours and compared with 316H stainless steel.
